meta.title: Always open, never enough hands: the strain on Japan's convenience stores
meta.deck: Japan's corner shops pay bills, post parcels and print documents at three in the morning. Keeping them that way is getting harder.
meta.note: 这是一篇仿《经济学人》风格的原创练习文章，不是真实外刊的转载。文中的事实是概括性描述，仅供语言学习，请不要当作引用来源。

sents.en: Always open, never enough hands: the strain on Japan's convenience stores
sents.zh: 永不打烊，却总缺人手：日本便利店的压力
notes: hands 在这里指“人手、干活的人”，和中文的“人手”是同一个比喻。
the strain on sth：……承受的压力、负担。strain 原意是绳子被拉紧，引申为长期的压力。
冒号前是两个对立的短语：always open 和 never enough hands，一句话点出矛盾。

sents.en: Japan's corner shops pay bills, post parcels and print documents at three in the morning.
sents.zh: 日本街角的小店，凌晨三点也能帮你缴费、寄包裹、打印文件。
notes: corner shop：街角小店，英式说法，指社区里卖日用品的小店。
post 作动词是英式用法，“邮寄”，美式多用 mail。
主语是店，但缴费、寄件的其实是顾客。这种把服务说成店在做的写法，强调店能办的事多。

sents.en: Keeping them that way is getting harder as the people who staff them grow scarce.
sents.zh: 可随着店员越来越难找，要让它们保持这样正变得越来越难。
notes: Keeping them that way 是动名词短语作主语，that way 指上一句描述的样子。
staff 作动词：为……配备人员、在……上班。the people who staff them = 在店里上班的人。
grow scarce：变得稀缺。grow + 形容词表示逐渐变化，类似 grow old、grow dark。

sents.en: It is two o'clock in the morning in a quiet suburb of Osaka, and the only lights on the street belong to a convenience store.
sents.zh: 大阪一个安静的郊区，凌晨两点，整条街唯一亮着的灯属于一家便利店。
notes: 开头用一个具体场景引入，是这类特稿常见的写法。
suburb：郊区、城市周边的住宅区。
belong to：属于。the only lights ... belong to a convenience store，用“灯属于便利店”来写整条街只有便利店还开着。

sents.en: Inside, a lone clerk is restocking rice balls, while a taxi driver warms up a bento in the microwave and a student pays her phone bill at the till.
sents.zh: 店里，一个店员独自在补货饭团；一位出租车司机在用微波炉热便当，一个学生在收银台交手机费。
notes: lone：独自的、唯一的，常放在名词前，如 a lone clerk、a lone tree。
restock：给货架补货。re- 表示“再次”，stock 是“存货”。
while 连接同时发生的几件事，三个人各做各的，画面很满。
the till：收银台、收银机，英式说法；at the till = 在收银台。

sents.en: Nobody seems to find any of this remarkable.
sents.zh: 没有人觉得这有什么稀奇。
notes: find + 宾语 + 形容词：觉得某事怎么样。find it strange = 觉得奇怪。
any of this 指上一句描述的一切。
remarkable：值得注意的、不寻常的。短句收尾，把前面的热闹落到“理所当然”上。

sents.en: Japan has more than 55,000 of these shops, known locally as konbini, or roughly one for every 2,200 people.
sents.zh: 日本有五万五千多家这样的店，当地人叫它们“konbini”，大约每两千二百人就有一家。
notes: known locally as：当地叫作……。过去分词短语作补充说明。
konbini 是日语 convenience 的缩略说法。
or 在这里不是“或者”，而是“换句话说”，把总数换算成更直观的比例。
one for every N people：每 N 个人有一个。

sents.en: They began as copies of American corner stores in the 1970s, but have since grown into something closer to a public utility.
sents.zh: 它们在上世纪七十年代起步时是在模仿美国的街角商店，后来却发展成了更接近公共服务设施的东西。
notes: begin as：起初是……；grow into：逐渐长成、发展成……。前后对照，写出变化。
have since grown：since 作副词，“从那以后”，配现在完成时。
public utility：公用事业，指水、电、燃气这类人人离不开的服务。

sents.en: Customers can pay taxes and utility bills, send and collect parcels, buy concert tickets, withdraw cash and print official documents such as residence certificates.
sents.zh: 顾客可以在这里交税、交水电煤气费，寄取包裹，买演唱会门票，取现金，还能打印住民票这类官方文件。
notes: utility bills：水电煤气等账单。
collect：领取。collect a parcel = 取包裹，英式常用；美式多说 pick up。
withdraw cash：取现金。withdraw 原意是“收回、撤回”。
一长串动词短语并列，用来列举便利店能办的事。

sents.en: After earthquakes, the chains are among the first to reopen, and local governments count on them to keep food and water flowing.
sents.zh: 地震过后，这些连锁店总是最早恢复营业的一批，地方政府也指望它们保证食物和饮用水的供应不断。
notes: among the first to do sth：最早做某事的那一批之一。
count on sb to do sth：指望、依靠某人做某事。
keep sth flowing：让……持续流动、不中断。flow 用来比喻物资的供应。

sents.en: All of this rests on a business model that leaves very little room for error.
sents.zh: 这一切都建立在一种几乎容不得出错的经营模式上。
notes: rest on：建立在……之上、取决于……。
business model：商业模式、经营模式。
room for error：出错的余地。leave little room for error = 几乎不允许出错。

sents.en: Most stores are run by franchise owners, who pay the parent company a hefty share of their gross profit in return for its brand, its supply chain and its data.
sents.zh: 大多数门店由加盟店主经营。他们把毛利的一大块交给总部，换来总部的品牌、供应链和数据。
notes: franchise owner：加盟店主。franchise 指特许经营权。
parent company：母公司，这里指连锁总部。
a hefty share of：相当大的一部分。hefty 原指“又大又重的”。
in return for：作为……的交换、换取。

sents.en: Lorries deliver fresh food several times a day, so shelves rarely sit empty and little is left to go to waste.
sents.zh: 货车每天送几次新鲜食品，所以货架很少空着，剩下来要浪费掉的东西也很少。
notes: lorry：卡车，英式用法；美式说 truck。
sit empty：空着、闲置着。sit 在这里表示处于某种状态，不是“坐”。
go to waste：被浪费掉。little is left to go to waste = 几乎没有剩下要浪费的。

sents.en: The system is famously efficient, but it depends on someone being behind the counter around the clock.
sents.zh: 这套体系的高效出了名，可它要靠柜台后面一天二十四小时都有人。
notes: famously：出了名地、众所周知地。
depend on someone being ...：depend on 后面接“名词 + 动名词”，意思是“依赖某人处于某种状态”。
around the clock：昼夜不停、二十四小时。英式也常说 round the clock。

sents.en: That someone is increasingly hard to find.
sents.zh: 而这个“有人”越来越难找。
notes: That someone 接住上一句的 someone，加上 that 变成“那个人”，承上启下。
increasingly：越来越，修饰形容词或动词。

sents.en: Japan's working-age population has been shrinking for three decades, and part-time jobs that pay little and involve night shifts are the first to go unfilled.
sents.zh: 日本的劳动年龄人口已经连续三十年在减少，工资低、又要上夜班的兼职工作最先招不到人。
notes: working-age population：劳动年龄人口，一般指十五到六十四岁。
has been shrinking for three decades：现在完成进行时，强调一直持续到现在。
night shift：夜班。
go unfilled：（职位）空着没人填补。go + 形容词表示变成某种（通常不好的）状态。

sents.en: Many owners now cover the gaps themselves, working 12-hour shifts for weeks on end.
sents.zh: 许多店主只好自己顶上空缺，一连几周每天上十二个小时的班。
notes: cover the gaps：填补空缺。cover 有“代班、顶替”的意思，如 cover for a colleague。
working 12-hour shifts 是伴随状语，说明他们怎么填补空缺。
for weeks on end：一连好几周、连续几周。on end 表示“连续不断”。

sents.en: A few years ago, an owner who shut his shop overnight without permission, saying he could no longer stay awake, briefly became a national talking point.
sents.zh: 几年前，一位店主没经总部同意就在夜里关了店，说自己实在熬不住了，一时成了全国热议的话题。
notes: 主干是 an owner ... became a national talking point，中间的 who 从句和 saying 短语都在说明这个店主。
without permission：未经许可。这里指没有得到总部同意。
no longer：不再。could no longer stay awake = 再也撑不住不睡了。
talking point：话题、大家议论的事。

sents.en: The chains have responded in several ways.
sents.zh: 连锁总部想了几种办法应对。
notes: respond：回应、作出反应。这是一个过渡句，引出下面的几种做法。

sents.en: Foreign workers, many of them students from Vietnam, Nepal and China, now make up a large share of staff in big cities.
sents.zh: 在大城市，外国员工如今占了店员的很大一部分，其中不少是来自越南、尼泊尔和中国的留学生。
notes: many of them students ...：独立主格结构，补充说明 foreign workers，相当于 and many of them are students。
make up：构成、占。make up a large share of = 占……的很大比例。
staff 在这里是集合名词，“员工”。

sents.en: Self-checkout machines are spreading, and some stores have experimented with closing at night or running without staff at all.
sents.zh: 自助收银机越来越普及，有些店还试过夜里关门，甚至完全不用店员。
notes: self-checkout：自助结账。
spread：扩散、普及，进行时表示正在变多。
experiment with sth / doing sth：试着做、尝试。
run 在这里是“（店）运营”，running without staff = 无人经营。

sents.en: Yet every shortcut chips away at what made the konbini indispensable in the first place: a real person, ready to help, at any hour.
sents.zh: 可每一种省事的办法，都在一点点削弱便利店当初让人离不开的东西：任何时候都有一个真人在那里，随时可以帮忙。
notes: shortcut：捷径，这里指省人力的办法。
chip away at：一点一点地削弱、蚕食，像用凿子一点点凿掉。
what made the konbini indispensable 是名词性从句，作 at 的宾语。indispensable = 不可或缺的。
in the first place：最初、原本。冒号后面解释 what 到底指什么。

sents.en: There is a lesson here for other rich countries that are ageing fast.
sents.zh: 这对其他正快速老龄化的富裕国家是个教训。
notes: There is a lesson here for ...：这里有值得……借鉴的地方，常用于文章收尾。
ageing：老龄化，英式拼写；美式拼作 aging。

sents.en: Services that people take for granted are often propped up by cheap, flexible labour that is quietly disappearing.
sents.zh: 人们视为理所当然的服务，往往是靠廉价、灵活的劳动力撑起来的，而这样的劳动力正在悄悄消失。
notes: take sth for granted：把……视为理所当然。这里 sth 是前面的 services，所以 take 后面没有宾语。
prop up：支撑、撑住，常指撑住本来会倒的东西。
labour：劳动力，英式拼写；美式拼作 labor。
两个 that 从句分别修饰 services 和 labour。

sents.en: Japan's convenience stores may be the first place where the shortfall shows up, but they are unlikely to be the last.
sents.zh: 日本的便利店可能是最早显出人手短缺的地方，但不太可能是最后一个。
notes: shortfall：短缺、缺口。
show up：显现、露出来。
the first ... the last：首尾对照，意思是这种问题以后会在更多地方出现。

sents.en: Sooner or later, customers may have to accept that convenience, like everything else, has a price.
sents.zh: 迟早，顾客可能得接受一个事实：便利和别的东西一样，也是要付出代价的。
notes: sooner or later：迟早。
like everything else 是插入语，夹在主语和谓语之间。
have a price：有代价。convenience 一语双关，既指便利，也指便利店。

vocab.note: hand 指“干活的人”时多用复数，常见于 farm hands、extra hands、short of hands。All hands on deck! = 所有人都来帮忙。

ex.en: We need more [[hands]] for the harvest.
ex.zh: 收庄稼需要更多人手。

ex.en: The kitchen is short of [[hands]] on Fridays.
ex.zh: 厨房每到周五就缺人手。

vocab.note: strain 指长期的压力、负担。put a strain on sth = 给……造成压力；under strain = 承受着压力。

ex.en: The heatwave put a huge [[strain on]] the power grid.
ex.zh: 热浪给电网造成了巨大压力。

ex.en: Long hours are taking a toll; you can see the [[strain on]] her face.
ex.zh: 长时间工作让她吃不消，脸上都能看出疲惫。

vocab.note: 英式用 post，美式用 mail。名词 the post 也指邮件或邮政系统：It came in the post. = 这是寄来的。

ex.en: I [[posted]] the birthday card on Monday.
ex.zh: 我周一把生日贺卡寄出去了。

ex.en: Could you [[post]] this letter on your way to work?
ex.zh: 你上班路上能帮我寄一下这封信吗？

vocab.note: staff 作动词，常见被动：The desk is staffed 24 hours a day. 作名词时是集合名词“员工”。

ex.en: The help desk is [[staffed]] by volunteers.
ex.zh: 服务台由志愿者值守。

ex.en: It is hard to [[staff]] a hospital at night.
ex.zh: 夜里很难给医院排够人手。

vocab.note: grow + 形容词表示慢慢变成某种状态：grow old、grow dark、grow tired。scarce = 稀少的、不够的。

ex.en: Water [[grew scarce]] as the summer went on.
ex.zh: 随着夏天过去，水越来越少。

ex.en: Cheap flats are [[growing scarce]] in the city centre.
ex.zh: 市中心便宜的公寓越来越难找。

vocab.note: belong to 不用进行时。The book belongs to me. 也可以说某物“应该在某处”：Where does this belong?

ex.en: This umbrella [[belongs to]] my sister.
ex.zh: 这把伞是我妹妹的。

ex.en: The land once [[belonged to]] the church.
ex.zh: 这块地以前归教会所有。

vocab.note: re- 表示“再次”，stock 是“存货”。restock the shelves = 给货架补货。

ex.en: Staff [[restock]] the shelves every night.
ex.zh: 店员每天晚上补货。

ex.en: The shop has not [[restocked]] since the storm.
ex.zh: 暴风雨过后这家店一直没补货。

vocab.note: 英式说 till，美式说 register 或 checkout。at the till = 在收银台；pay at the till = 在收银台付款。

ex.en: Please pay at [[the till]] by the door.
ex.zh: 请到门口的收银台付款。

ex.en: There was a long queue at [[the till]].
ex.zh: 收银台前排着长队。

vocab.note: known as = 被称为。中间加 locally 表示“当地人这么叫”。也可说 known to friends as（朋友们叫他……）。

ex.en: The hill, [[known locally as]] the Sleeping Giant, is easy to climb.
ex.zh: 这座山当地人叫“睡巨人”，很好爬。

ex.en: He runs a café [[known locally as]] the Blue Door.
ex.zh: 他开了一家当地人叫“蓝门”的咖啡馆。

vocab.zh: 每 N 个人就有一个
vocab.note: 表示比例的常用说法。也可说 one in every ten（每十个里有一个）。

ex.en: There is a doctor [[for every]] 500 residents.
ex.zh: 每五百个居民有一名医生。

ex.en: The school has [[one for every]] class.
ex.zh: 学校每个班都配了一个。

vocab.note: grow into 强调慢慢变成另一种东西：The village has grown into a town. 也可说孩子“长大到穿得下”：He will grow into the coat.

ex.en: The small café has [[grown into]] a chain of 30 shops.
ex.zh: 那家小咖啡馆已经发展成有三十家店的连锁品牌。

ex.en: The hobby slowly [[grew into]] a business.
ex.zh: 这个爱好慢慢变成了一门生意。

vocab.note: utility 单用也可以指水电燃气这类服务，utility bills = 水电煤气费。文中说便利店“像公用事业”，是说人人离不开它。

ex.en: Water is treated as a [[public utility]] in most countries.
ex.zh: 在大多数国家，供水被当作公用事业。

ex.en: For many people, the internet is now a [[public utility]].
ex.zh: 对很多人来说，网络如今就是一种公用事业。

vocab.note: 英式常说 collect a parcel / collect the children from school；美式更常用 pick up。

ex.en: You can [[collect]] your order from the shop after five.
ex.zh: 五点以后可以到店里取你订的东西。

ex.en: I [[collected]] the kids from school.
ex.zh: 我去学校接了孩子。

vocab.note: withdraw 原意是“撤回、收回”。withdraw money from an account = 从账户取钱，名词 withdrawal。

ex.en: I need to [[withdraw cash]] before the trip.
ex.zh: 出发前我得取点现金。

ex.en: He [[withdrew]] £200 from the machine.
ex.zh: 他从取款机取了两百英镑。

vocab.note: count on sb / count on sb to do sth。You can count on me. = 你可以靠我。同义：rely on, depend on。

ex.en: You can [[count on]] her to be on time.
ex.zh: 你可以放心，她一定准时。

ex.en: We were [[counting on]] good weather for the picnic.
ex.zh: 我们本来指望野餐那天天气好。

vocab.note: rest on 的主语常是计划、论点、成功等抽象的东西：The plan rests on one assumption.

ex.en: The whole plan [[rests on]] one big guess.
ex.zh: 整个计划都建立在一个大胆的猜测上。

ex.en: Her case [[rested on]] a single witness.
ex.zh: 她的说法全靠一个证人。

vocab.note: room 作不可数名词时是“空间、余地”。little / no room for error = 几乎不能出错；room for improvement = 有改进的余地。

ex.en: With only ten minutes left, there is no [[room for error]].
ex.zh: 只剩十分钟了，一点也不能出错。

ex.en: Pilots are trained because there is little [[room for error]].
ex.zh: 飞行员要经过训练，因为几乎容不得出错。

vocab.note: franchise：特许经营（权）。franchisee 也是加盟商，franchisor 是授权方，也就是总部。

ex.en: Most [[franchise owners]] work in their own shops.
ex.zh: 大多数加盟店主都在自己店里干活。

ex.en: She became a [[franchise owner]] after 20 years as a manager.
ex.zh: 当了二十年经理之后，她自己开了一家加盟店。

vocab.note: hefty 原指又大又重，也常修饰钱：a hefty fine（一大笔罚款）、a hefty bill（一大笔账单）。

ex.en: Rent takes a [[hefty share]] of my salary.
ex.zh: 房租占了我工资的一大块。

ex.en: He paid a [[hefty]] fine for speeding.
ex.zh: 他因为超速交了一大笔罚款。

vocab.note: in return for sth = 换取某物；单独用 in return = 作为回报：He helped me, and I paid him in return.

ex.en: She walks the neighbour's dog [[in return for]] free lunches.
ex.zh: 她帮邻居遛狗，换免费的午饭吃。

ex.en: They got free rent [[in return for]] fixing the house.
ex.zh: 他们帮忙修房子，换来了免交房租。

vocab.note: 常用于否定或劝说：Don't let the food go to waste. = 别浪费食物。

ex.en: Don't let all that food [[go to waste]].
ex.zh: 别让这么多吃的浪费掉。

ex.en: Half the vegetables [[went to waste]] last week.
ex.zh: 上周一半的菜都浪费了。

vocab.note: sit 在这里表示“处于某种状态”。类似说法：sit unused（闲置不用）、sit idle（闲着）。

ex.en: The flat [[sat empty]] for two years.
ex.zh: 那套公寓空置了两年。

ex.en: Thousands of offices now [[sit empty]] in the city.
ex.zh: 如今城里有成千上万间办公室空着。

vocab.note: famously + 形容词：famously shy（出了名的害羞）。也可放在句首：Famously, he never gave interviews.

ex.en: The trains are [[famously]] punctual.
ex.zh: 这里的火车准点是出了名的。

ex.en: He was [[famously]] bad at remembering names.
ex.zh: 他记不住人名是出了名的。

vocab.note: 也说 round the clock。作形容词时加连字符：round-the-clock care（全天候护理）。

ex.en: Nurses work [[around the clock]] in this ward.
ex.zh: 这个病房的护士全天轮班。

ex.en: The team worked [[round the clock]] to fix the bug.
ex.zh: 团队连轴转修这个漏洞。

vocab.note: increasingly + 形容词 / 动词：increasingly popular、increasingly worried。比 more and more 更书面。

ex.en: Flats in the city are [[increasingly]] expensive.
ex.zh: 城里的公寓越来越贵。

ex.en: People [[increasingly]] shop online.
ex.zh: 人们越来越多地在网上购物。

vocab.note: 一般指十五到六十四岁的人。working-age 作定语时加连字符：working-age adults。

ex.en: The country's [[working-age population]] is falling.
ex.zh: 这个国家的劳动年龄人口在减少。

ex.en: A shrinking [[working-age population]] means fewer taxpayers.
ex.zh: 劳动年龄人口减少，意味着纳税人变少。

vocab.note: go + 带 un- 的过去分词，表示某事没有发生：go unnoticed（没被注意到）、go unpaid（没拿到钱）。

ex.en: Many teaching jobs [[go unfilled]] every year.
ex.zh: 每年都有很多教师岗位招不到人。

ex.en: The post [[went unfilled]] for six months.
ex.zh: 这个职位空了六个月。

vocab.note: shift 是轮班。work the night shift = 上夜班；day shift = 白班。

ex.en: She works the [[night shift]] at the hospital.
ex.zh: 她在医院上夜班。

ex.en: [[Night shifts]] are paid a little more.
ex.zh: 夜班工资稍高一点。

vocab.note: cover 有“顶替、代班”的意思：Can you cover for me on Friday? = 周五你能替我上班吗？

ex.en: Volunteers [[cover the gaps]] when staff are off sick.
ex.zh: 员工生病请假时，由志愿者顶上。

ex.en: We hired temps to [[cover the gap]] over the summer.
ex.zh: 我们招了临时工来填补暑期的空缺。

vocab.note: on end 表示连续不断，也可以说 for hours on end、for days on end。

ex.en: It rained [[for weeks on end]].
ex.zh: 雨一连下了好几周。

ex.en: He played video games [[for hours on end]].
ex.zh: 他一连几个小时打游戏。

vocab.note: talking point 指大家议论的事，也指发言要点：the minister's talking points（部长的发言要点）。

ex.en: The new stadium became a big [[talking point]] in town.
ex.zh: 新体育场成了城里热议的话题。

ex.en: Her dress was the main [[talking point]] of the evening.
ex.zh: 她的裙子是当晚大家谈论最多的话题。

vocab.note: make up 有很多意思，表示“构成”时常接比例：Women make up half the team. 被动：be made up of = 由……组成。

ex.en: Students [[make up]] most of the audience.
ex.zh: 观众大部分是学生。

ex.en: Rent [[makes up]] a third of my spending.
ex.zh: 房租占我开支的三分之一。

vocab.note: experiment with sth / doing sth：带着试一试的心态去做。名词 experiment = 实验。

ex.en: The café [[experimented with]] opening on Sundays.
ex.zh: 那家咖啡馆试过周日营业。

ex.en: Chefs love to [[experiment with]] new flavours.
ex.zh: 厨师们喜欢尝试新口味。

vocab.note: chip 是“削下碎片”。chip away at sth 指一点一点削弱、蚕食：chip away at trust（一点点消磨信任）。

ex.en: Small lies [[chip away at]] trust.
ex.zh: 一个个小谎言会慢慢消磨信任。

ex.en: Rising prices are [[chipping away at]] people's savings.
ex.zh: 物价上涨正一点点吃掉人们的积蓄。

vocab.note: in- 否定 + dispense with（免掉、不用）+ -able，字面是“免不掉的”。同义 essential，比 important 更强。

ex.en: A good map is [[indispensable]] on this hike.
ex.zh: 走这条徒步路线，一张好地图必不可少。

ex.en: She made herself [[indispensable]] to the team.
ex.zh: 她让自己在团队里不可或缺。

vocab.note: 常用来追问最初的原因：Why did you buy it in the first place? = 你当初为什么要买它？

ex.en: Why did you agree to it [[in the first place]]?
ex.zh: 你当初为什么要答应？

ex.en: The rules that made the town safe [[in the first place]] are now being dropped.
ex.zh: 当初让小镇安全的那些规定，现在正在被取消。

vocab.note: 英式拼写 ageing，美式 aging。an ageing population = 老龄化的人口；age 作动词 = 变老。

ex.en: Europe has an [[ageing]] population.
ex.zh: 欧洲人口正在老龄化。

ex.en: The [[ageing]] bridge needs repairs.
ex.zh: 那座老旧的桥需要维修。

vocab.note: take sth for granted；宾语长或是从句时可以说 take it for granted that ...。也常用于人：Don't take your parents for granted.

ex.en: We [[take for granted]] that the lights will come on.
ex.zh: 我们理所当然地认为灯会亮。

ex.en: Clean water is easy to take [[for granted]].
ex.zh: 干净的水很容易被当作理所当然。

vocab.note: prop 是支柱。prop up 常指撑住本来会倒的东西，也用于经济：prop up a failing bank（救助一家快倒的银行）。

ex.en: The old wall is [[propped up]] with wooden beams.
ex.zh: 那堵旧墙用木梁撑着。

ex.en: The government spent billions to [[prop up]] the airline.
ex.zh: 政府花了几十亿救助那家航空公司。

vocab.note: a shortfall in / of sth：……的缺口。常用于钱和人：a funding shortfall（资金缺口）、a staff shortfall（人手缺口）。

ex.en: The school faces a [[shortfall]] of ten teachers.
ex.zh: 这所学校缺十名老师。

ex.en: Taxes rose to cover the budget [[shortfall]].
ex.zh: 为了填补预算缺口，税涨了。

vocab.note: show up 也常指“到场、露面”：He didn't show up. 文中指问题“显现出来”。

ex.en: The damage only [[shows up]] under bright light.
ex.zh: 损坏只有在强光下才看得出来。

ex.en: Stress often [[shows up]] in your sleep.
ex.zh: 压力常常会反映在睡眠上。

vocab.note: 表示某事终究会发生。也可说 eventually。

ex.en: [[Sooner or later]], you will have to tell her.
ex.zh: 你迟早得告诉她。

ex.en: Everyone makes that mistake [[sooner or later]].
ex.zh: 每个人迟早都会犯这个错。

vocab.expr: among the first to do sth
vocab.zh: 最早做某事的那一批之一
vocab.note: among 表示“在一群之中”，所以说的是“最早的几个之一”，不一定是第一个。反过来可以说 among the last to do sth（最晚的那一批）。也可以不接动词：among the first in line（排在最前面的几个人里）。

ex.en: She was [[among the first to]] arrive at the party.
ex.zh: 她是最早到聚会的几个人之一。

ex.en: Our town was [[among the first to]] get fast internet.
ex.zh: 我们镇是最早通上高速网络的地方之一。

ex.en: Nurses are often [[among the first to]] notice a problem.
ex.zh: 护士往往是最早发现问题的人。

breakdown.en: Yet every shortcut chips away at what made the konbini indispensable in the first place: a real person, ready to help, at any hour.
points: 主干很短：every shortcut chips away at what ...，意思是“每一种省事的办法都在削弱……”。
what made the konbini indispensable in the first place 是名词性从句，作介词 at 的宾语。what = the thing that。
made + 宾语 + 形容词：使……变得……。made the konbini indispensable = 让便利店变得不可或缺。
冒号后面的 a real person, ready to help, at any hour 是对 what 的解释，用三个短语一层层说清楚：一个真人、随时愿意帮忙、什么时候都在。
开头的 Yet 是“然而”，和上一段的各种应对办法形成转折。
